T0613.title: Robot Swarm
T0613.definition: A system where multiple robots collaborate via communication and coordination protocols to accomplish tasks, with distributed perception, collaborative decision-making, and collective action, applied in warehouse, inspection, and military scenarios.
T0613.description: Robot swarms achieve tasks impossible for single robots via distributed collaboration, but introduce swarm-specific loss-of-control risks. Individual hijacked swarm members become byzantine nodes that send false information to break consensus; communication disruption desynchronizes the swarm; single-point failures are amplified by the swarm topology and are hard to stop via single-robot e-stop. The KARGU-2 lethal autonomous weapon system, per a UN report, had swarm-coordination and autonomous target-tracking capabilities in the 2020 Libya civil war. In multi-agent reinforcement learning, Gleave et al. proved an adversary can defeat SOTA RL policies by its own behavior alone. Swarm fault tolerance requires byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, member anomaly detection, and swarm-level e-stop.
T0613.usageExample: If one warehouse robot in a swarm is hijacked into a byzantine node sending false position information, it may cause path conflicts across the entire swarm, paralyzing operations.
